cineduct.sodium.quality.name: Video Quality
cineduct.sodium.quality.tooltip.auto: Picks a quality tier automatically from measured bandwidth: it climbs when the network is fast and drops a tier to stay smooth when it isn't. Recommended.
cineduct.sodium.quality.tooltip.360p: Standard definition. The lightest on bandwidth and decoding; use it on a poor connection.
cineduct.sodium.quality.tooltip.480p: A little sharper than 360p, still a low bitrate.
cineduct.sodium.quality.tooltip.720p: HD. The usual pick for most videos, balancing sharpness and bandwidth.
cineduct.sodium.quality.tooltip.720p60: 720p at 60 fps: smoother motion and games, at a noticeably higher bitrate.
cineduct.sodium.quality.tooltip.1080p: Full HD. Requires signing in; the high-bitrate version needs Premium.
cineduct.sodium.quality.tooltip.1080p60: Full HD at 60 fps. Usually requires Premium, and asks a bit more of the decoder.
cineduct.sodium.quality.tooltip.4k: Ultra HD (2160p). Requires Premium and is demanding to decode; keep In-process HW Decode on.
cineduct.sodium.quality.tooltip.8k: 8K. Bilibili mostly offers AV1 only, which nearly every GPU has to decode in software, so expect heavy stutter.
cineduct.sodium.quality.tooltip.unlimite: No cap: use the highest quality your account can get. Meant for Premium users on strong hardware.
cineduct.sodium.live_quality.name: Live Quality
cineduct.sodium.live_quality.tooltip.ori: The streamer's highest push quality, and Bilibili Live's default tier.
cineduct.sodium.live_quality.tooltip.blu: 1080p at a higher bitrate; only rooms that offer this transcode have it, otherwise it falls back automatically.
cineduct.sodium.live_quality.tooltip.smo: The lowest tier, lightest on bandwidth.
cineduct.sodium.zero_copy.name: Zero-copy Subprocess
cineduct.sodium.zero_copy.tooltip: Hands playback to a C++ subprocess: frames are decoded in the subprocess and bound straight as the GL texture through a DXGI shared texture (no CPU read-back), with audio going out via WASAPI. It does not conflict with In-process HW Decode: that path also decodes in hardware, it just copies frames back. Falls back to the in-process engine when unavailable. Experimental, off by default; applies to videos afterwards.
cineduct.sodium.hw_decode.name: In-process HW Decode
cineduct.sodium.hw_decode.tooltip: Whether the in-process Java engine decodes with d3d11va / dxva2 (on by default). With it off this path falls back to software decoding, which cannot keep up with 4K; it is only useful for working around driver glitches. It does not affect the zero-copy subprocess, which decodes in hardware on its own. Applies to videos opened afterwards.
cineduct.sodium.avoid_av1.name: Avoid AV1
cineduct.sodium.avoid_av1.tooltip: AV1 compresses best, but most GPUs cannot decode it in hardware, so it runs in software (4K AV1 can drop to single-digit FPS). Turning this on prefers H.264 / HEVC. Note: 8K is usually AV1-only, so 8K may become unavailable. Applies to videos opened afterwards.
cineduct.sodium.audio_track.name: Preferred Audio Track
cineduct.sodium.audio_track.tooltip.dolb: Prefer Dolby Atmos (E-AC-3), then Hi-Res lossless, then the highest-bitrate standard track. Needs Premium and a video that offers it; otherwise it falls back automatically.
cineduct.sodium.audio_track.tooltip.hire: Prefer Hi-Res lossless (FLAC), then Dolby, then the standard track. Requires Premium.
cineduct.sodium.audio_track.tooltip.best: Pick the highest-bitrate standard AAC track only. Best compatibility, no membership needed.
cineduct.sodium.av_offset.name: A/V Sync Offset
cineduct.sodium.av_offset.tooltip: Sound reaches your ears through HDMI, a receiver or a soundbar, so the picture tends to run ahead. Use positive values when the picture is fast and negative values when it lags, and adjust until they line up. Press Apply to affect the playing video immediately.
cineduct.sodium.max_delay.name: Max Server Sync Delay
cineduct.sodium.max_delay.tooltip: When the server syncs progress, if its target is ahead of your position by no more than this many seconds, playback fast-forwards inside already-buffered data (no reconnect, no buffer flush); beyond that it performs a real seek. Larger values reduce stutter, smaller values track the server more strictly. 0 still keeps a 1-second floor.
